nodes.label: architect agent (Opus, xhigh)
nodes.rationale: Owns complex changes end to end; diagnoses prior failed attempts before changing course; escalation target when builder fails.

nodes.label: builder agent (Sonnet, high)
nodes.rationale: Implements a clearly scoped 1-3 file change following an existing pattern; stops and reports instead of widening scope.

nodes.label: reviewer agent (Sonnet, high, read-only)
nodes.rationale: Reviews diffs against AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rules; style preferences are not findings and it must state when a change is fine.

nodes.label: scout agent (Haiku, read-only)
nodes.rationale: Answers one scoped lookup; queries the graphify graph first when present, never builds or updates it.

nodes.label: test-runner agent (Haiku)
nodes.rationale: Runs builds/test filters and returns only failures, keeping verbose output out of the main context; never fixes failures.

nodes.label: Cascade routing pattern (cheap first, escalate on failed verification)
nodes.norm_label: cascade routing pattern (cheap first, escalate on failed verification)
nodes.rationale: Beats a single frontier model on cost and quality; main risk is silent quality regression, so gate routing changes with an eval.

nodes.label: Coordinator habits
nodes.rationale: Editing agents run in the foreground because background agents auto-deny permission prompts and may report edits never made.

nodes.label: Escalation ladder (scout -> builder -> architect -> fable)
nodes.rationale: On failure climb one rung with the failure attached; two failures at the top rung means the task needs re-scoping. After fan-out run the full suite once since per-agent greens do not prove the combination.

nodes.label: Fan-out four independence checks (Step 3)
nodes.rationale: Fan out only when problems are independently understandable, cannot fix each other, share no files/resources, and are already localised; cap 3 to 5 concurrent agents.

nodes.label: Graph-first lookups via graphify
nodes.rationale: Before routing a lookup, check graphify-out/graph.json; query/explain/path/affected against the local graph, confirm INFERRED edges in code, fall back to grep on exit 4.

nodes.label: One code graph per project (graphify or Cortex)
nodes.norm_label: one code graph per project (graphify or cortex)
nodes.rationale: Use graphify when graphify-out/ exists, otherwise Cortex's code graph; never query both, because stacking two unconditional graph-first instruction blocks is warned against.

nodes.label: Agent/model/effort routing table (Step 2)
nodes.rationale: Single-shot code quality plateaus at high while xhigh agentic loops use fewer total tokens; Sonnet 5 medium matches Sonnet 4.6 high, so lower effort before switching model.

nodes.label: Task tier classification (Step 1)
nodes.rationale: When two tiers fit, take the cheaper one and rely on the escalation ladder.

nodes.label: Bug Fix via Reproducing Test
nodes.rationale: The reproducing test is proof of the fix and regression guard; a fix without one is a guess.

nodes.label: Delegating Test Runs to test-runner
nodes.rationale: Test output is the biggest context cost; send runs to the cheap test-runner agent asking for failures only, or pipe through tail/grep.

nodes.label: No Production Code Without a Failing Test
nodes.norm_label: no production code without a failing test
nodes.rationale: A test written after code passes immediately and proves nothing; code written before its test is deleted, not kept as reference.

nodes.label: Codex escalation ladder (luna -> terra -> sol -> gpt-6-astra)
nodes.norm_label: codex escalation ladder (luna -> terra -> sol -> gpt-6-astra)

nodes.label: Name the agent explicitly in the request
nodes.norm_label: name the agent explicitly in the request
nodes.rationale: Prevents Codex from falling back to built-in default/worker/explorer roles.

nodes.label: Codex agent/model/effort/sandbox routing table
nodes.rationale: OpenAI documents low for tool-driven search, high for complex debugging, xhigh for long agentic runs; GPT-5 benchmarks show ~23x token spread with flat quality on classification work.

nodes.label: Read-only sandbox locking for non-writing subagents
nodes.norm_label: read-only sandbox locking for non-writing subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagents inherit the parent's approval policy, so an approval-gated edit may be denied silently; keep edits in builder/architect and check with git diff.

nodes.label: External skills (not stored in repo)
nodes.rationale: External skill text is generated by the tool's own CLI and stamped with its version, so the installer installs the CLI and runs its install command instead of keeping a copy.

nodes.label: Vendor-grouped skill layout
nodes.rationale: Skills are grouped by the vendor whose tooling and model lineup they target; each skill is a folder with SKILL.md plus optional references/ and assets/.

nodes.label: Dedup judge (claude)
nodes.rationale: Biased to keep findings apart; four merge tiers; never merge across files; reruns safe via merged_into.

nodes.label: False-positive and severity judge (claude)
nodes.rationale: Prefer LIKELY_TP over LIKELY_FP when unsure; hardening gaps are TRUE_POSITIVE at LOW.

nodes.label: Finding file format (claude)
nodes.rationale: Workers never write severity, verdict or merge fields; judges add them.

nodes.label: disable-model-invocation: true
nodes.rationale: Prevents the model from starting the expensive audit on its own.

nodes.label: REPORT.md and REPORT.sarif artifacts (claude)
nodes.rationale: Partial runs must be disclosed; unjudged findings labelled unvalidated.

nodes.label: scope_subpath parameter (claude)
nodes.rationale: Findings filed only inside scope; rest of repo is read-only context for reachability.

nodes.label: worker_model parameter (claude)
nodes.rationale: Claude: haiku/sonnet/opus, judges sonnet+. OpenAI: Codex models gpt-5.6-luna/terra/sol, judges terra+.

nodes.label: policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false
nodes.rationale: Codex equivalent of disable-model-invocation: the audit runs only when the user names it.

nodes.rationale: Claude Code and Codex read the same marker, so both hosts share one store.

nodes.label: Claude Code lifecycle hooks (ambient memory)
nodes.rationale: On Claude Code the plugin hooks make memory ambient: session-start injection, auto-recall per prompt, capture, compaction checkpoint; on other hosts nothing happens unless tools are called.

nodes.label: Agent templates with placeholders
nodes.rationale: Templates are generic and contain <placeholders> (build command, test filter, project rules) that must be filled in per target repository; existing agents are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Background consolidation scheduling (Step 3)
nodes.rationale: No built-in scheduler; prefer a weekly Claude Code scheduled task; never more than weekly since consolidate's staleness threshold is six days.

nodes.label: Memory-moment decision (Step 1)
nodes.rationale: Search for questions about the past; write only decisions whose reason will not survive in the diff; the repo is authoritative when the answer is derivable from code.

nodes.label: Wrong/stale memory remediation (Step 4)
nodes.rationale: Deletion is the last option: rate_memory for ranking, supersede outdated decisions, soft forget for wrong ones, hard forget only for data that must not exist on disk.

nodes.label: Query habits (question not keywords, filters, provenance, supersession)
nodes.norm_label: query habits (question not keywords, filters, provenance, supersession)

nodes.label: Supersede rather than delete
nodes.rationale: Corrections demote the old memory and keep the chain as an audit trail; a corrected chain teaches, a hole does not.

nodes.label: Tuning cost guidance
nodes.rationale: Lower builder effort to medium before switching to a cheaper model; never spawn more agents than independent questions; keep file-editing agents in the foreground or workspace-write sandbox, everything else read-only.

nodes.label: Codex native lean plugin vs direct MCP registration
nodes.norm_label: codex native lean plugin vs direct mcp registration
nodes.rationale: Neither option adds Claude Code's lifecycle hooks, so recall, writes and consolidation happen only when explicitly called; direct registration exposes all 57 tools as mcp__cortex__<tool>.

nodes.label: Excalidraw Binding Rules Table
nodes.rationale: Validator warns on one-sided bindings and errors on unknown ids.

nodes.label: Two-sided Binding Rule
nodes.rationale: Arrow start/endBinding plus shape boundElements; text containerId plus container boundElements.

nodes.label: Conceptual vs Technical Depth
nodes.rationale: Technical diagrams need researched real names and evidence artifacts; never invent plausible payloads.

nodes.label: Behavior-to-Visual-Pattern Mapping (fan-out, funnel, tree, timeline, cycle...)
nodes.norm_label: behavior-to-visual-pattern mapping (fan-out, funnel, tree, timeline, cycle...)

nodes.label: Semantic Color Encoding (dark stroke + light fill)
nodes.norm_label: semantic color encoding (dark stroke + light fill)
nodes.rationale: Single place defining colors; change hex values here to rebrand; color encodes meaning per category.

nodes.label: Diagram That Argues (argue, don't display)
nodes.rationale: Structure should carry the idea, not only labels; adapted from coleam00's excalidraw-diagram-skill.

nodes.label: Education Test
nodes.rationale: A reader should learn something concrete (real format, event, command), not only that boxes connect.

nodes.label: Isomorphism Test
nodes.rationale: With all text removed, the diagram shape should still convey the concept.

nodes.label: Minimal Containers Rule (<30% boxed text)
nodes.rationale: Free-floating text by default; equal card grids say 'list', not argument; size encodes rank; whitespace is emphasis.

nodes.label: Mandatory Render-and-Inspect Loop
nodes.rationale: Validate, render to PNG, inspect against design, fix and re-render 2-4 rounds; if render impossible run --check and say layout not visually verified.

nodes.label: Section-by-section JSON Authoring
nodes.rationale: Hand-write JSON, never delegate or script it; single giant writes truncate and get sloppy.

nodes.label: Post-refactor Six-test Failure Example (abort/batch/approval)
nodes.rationale: Six failures in three files split into three independent domains; three builder agents fixed them in one message without touching the same file; context for one was not re-billed for the others.

nodes.label: Worktree Isolation for File Overlap
nodes.rationale: When domains touch neighbouring files, isolate each agent in a git worktree and merge afterwards, or serialize.

nodes.label: Mutation Check
nodes.rationale: Imagine realistic bugs (wrong constant/branch, missing side effect); at least one test must fail for each.

nodes.label: workspace-write Sandbox for Editing Subagents
nodes.rationale: Codex variant: editing subagents need a workspace-write sandbox and disjoint file sets; Codex runs subagents spawned in one request concurrently and waits for all.

nodes.label: Concurrency Cap and Waves (3-5 agents)
nodes.rationale: Cap at number of independent domains and 3-5 in practice (router rule, Codex thread limit); more domains run in waves.

nodes.label: Foreground Rule for Editing Agents
nodes.rationale: Background agents auto-deny permission prompts and may report edits they never made, so file-editing agents run with run_in_background false.

nodes.label: Split by Independent Domains
nodes.rationale: Group failures by what they touch, not count; pairwise check 'if this is fixed, can the other still fail?' merges dependent problems.

nodes.label: Integrate and Verify (combined full-suite run)
nodes.rationale: Per-agent greens do not prove the combination; run full suite once, check for overlapping edits and spot-check each agent. A combined failure means the domains were not independent.

nodes.label: Parallelism Criteria (is it really parallel)
nodes.rationale: Parallelize only if 2+ problems are independently understandable, fixing one cannot fix another, no shared files/resources, and the problem is already known; exploratory work stays in one thread.

nodes.label: Self-contained Agent Brief (scope/context/goal/constraints/output)
nodes.rationale: Each agent sees nothing else, so the brief must carry real errors, repro command, root-cause goal, forbidden paths and exact return format.

nodes.label: Single-message Dispatch
nodes.rationale: All agent calls in the same message run concurrently; one per message serializes them.

nodes.label: Every Test Targets a Specific Bug
nodes.norm_label: every test targets a specific bug

nodes.label: Green: Minimum Code
nodes.rationale: No extra options or generality the test does not demand.

nodes.label: Verify Red (fail for the right reason)
nodes.norm_label: verify red (fail for the right reason)
nodes.rationale: Failure must come from missing behavior, not typos/imports/compile errors; a passing new test means the test is wrong.
